sources_considered.why: Primary evaluation of many image classifiers and robustness interventions under related testing conditions.
Primary language-inference experiments examine both targeted augmentation and transfer to withheld cases.
Useful synthesis of shortcut learning, but the direct experiments provide stronger evidence.
Defines the claim; it cannot independently establish its truth.

receipt.public_excerpt: most current techniques provide no robustness

evidence_items.explanation: The study evaluates 204 ImageNet models across 213 conditions and finds limited transfer from synthetic robustness tests to natural changes. It also identifies an exception: larger, more diverse training datasets sometimes improve transfer.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; R. Thomas McCoy, Ellie Pavlick, and Tal Linzen

receipt.public_excerpt: near-zero performance across all three heuristics.

evidence_items.explanation: Models successful on MNLI fail on related inference examples, and targeted augmentation still leaves some withheld categories unsolved. The authors also report successful transfer to other categories and an external dataset, limiting any stronger claim that targeted training never generalizes.

unresolved_gaps: These studies establish a recurring pattern, not a numerical estimate of its prevalence across the entire AI field.
They do not establish that the particular GPT-4o improvements discussed in the post resulted from targeted patches or memorization.
